name: Mastek Ltd
title: Mastek Ltd - 523704 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Mastek Q4 FY26 revenue rose 3.6% QoQ to INR938 crore with EBITDA steady at 16.1%; 12-month backlog up 13.5% YoY in USD.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was described by management as a stable quarter: USD revenue of $103.5 million was up 1.4% QoQ (flat in constant currency), and EBITDA held at 16.1% despite a $1.1 million salary increase. FY26 revenue grew 7% YoY in INR to INR3,699 crore, with EBITDA flat at 15.8%. Reported PAT was hit by a INR23.7 crore exceptional Labour Code true-up in Q4 (INR6.4 crore in Q3), which management moved below EBITDA and which restated Q3 EBITDA to 16.8%. Management guided to FY27 growth above FY26 but declined to give a numerical target.

financial_highlights.change: +1.4% QoQ in USD; +3.6% QoQ and YoY in INR; flat QoQ in constant currency (+0.3%)
Stable; salary hike impact ~1.1% offset by 0.8% forex tailwind and cost efficiencies
-0.7% QoQ, affected by Labour Code true-up

+3.1% YoY in USD; +7% YoY in INR

segments.name: UK & Europe
segments.commentary: Grew ~11% in GBP and 21.8% in INR in FY26; UK EBITDA about 20% in Q4. Healthcare (NHS-led) grew ~24% in USD and 90%+ in INR in FY26. Q4 UK sequentially up, 12-month backlog up significantly.

segments.name: North America (US)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat QoQ on project ramp-downs; EBITDA margin down YoY and QoQ on revenue stabilisation and wage hikes. Order book up sequentially for a second straight quarter, but 12-month backlog has not risen significantly. Management expects FY27 growth, with fixed-bid above 50-55% of the region's business.

segments.name: AMEA (APAC & Middle East)
segments.commentary: Grew sequentially in Q4 and recognised ~$0.5 million of WAR-related revenue deferred from Q2. Margin down YoY and QoQ on flat revenue and wage hikes. Middle East faces short-term geopolitical headwinds; new decision-making has slowed.

segments.name: Financial services
segments.commentary: Described as the star of the quarter; ramp-up from large North American BFSI wins and UK/AMEA FS orders. Management said FCA deal reached 60+ onsite resources and will be fully ramped by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Sequential dip in Q4 from project timing gaps (live transitions in UK and US) with new projects yet to start; management expects recovery as new programmes ramp.

segments.name: Retail & manufacturing
segments.commentary: Stable, with a timing dip of around 2% in the vertical in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give numerical guidance; expects FY27 to be a growth year and better than FY26, with revenue growth to track the 12-month backlog.
EBITDA margin expected to hold at 16% to 16.1% in the coming period, balancing AI-led efficiency against pricing pressure and new AI investment.
Effective tax rate expected at 24.5% to 24.7% in future quarters.
Headcount growth expected to be slower than revenue growth, so revenue per resource should rise.
North America expected to show positive growth in FY27; AMEA expected to turn to growth in FY27, subject to geopolitical developments.
DSO expected to hold near the 73-day level in the long term, with plus or minus a few days in the short term.
M&A to focus on vertical and domain capabilities; AI investments to be smaller, with larger partnerships.
capex_capacity: Utilisation improved to 80% in Q4 FY26, up 3.3pp QoQ.
Headcount 4,730 at Q4 end, up 54 QoQ, with revenue per resource up more than 12% in FY26.
Two Indian entities merged (Mastek Enterprise Solutions Pvt Ltd into Mastek Ltd) to simplify structure; FY25 balance sheet restated, with receivables and unbilled reclassified.
Management is evaluating M&A and AI partnerships with the rising cash balance (INR938 crore), with an emphasis on domain-focused assets.
demand_pricing: Renewals are priced very competitively; earlier renewals were done at 10-15% discounts and could go much higher, driven by AI-enabled productivity gains.
Management is shifting from T&M to outcome-based and fixed-bid contracts; fixed-bid is about 40% of company revenue.
Order book mix: UK public sector and framework orders run 3 to 5 years; Salesforce and Oracle project orders run 1 to 1.5 years.
AI-led deals (70-80% AI usage in delivery) are early and small, with average deal size around $1 million; AI share of order book rose from about 3% to 9% over two quarters, per an analyst's figures.
Private sector is about 40% of group business and about 30% of UK business; healthcare and financial services are the growth sectors there.
Top 30-40 customers contribute 65-70% of revenue; management is deliberately churning smaller, non-strategic accounts.
Oracle Health and AI transformation work is seen as a pipeline for AI-led back-office and front-office programmes.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY26 low growth be followed by a stronger first half of FY27, and will management give a growth number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 would be a growth year with better performance than FY26 but declined to give a numerical guidance, citing an unstable macro and AI-led pricing pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the average effective tax rate would be 24.5% to 24.7%; the Q4 rate was lower because of a past-year assessment provision reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off in AMEA from deferred WAR revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, about $0.5 million of WAR revenue deferred from Q2 was recognised in Q4; new AMEA decision-making has slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did US and AMEA margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: North America saw pressure from revenue stabilisation and the wage hike; AMEA had flat revenue and the wage hike, with the full wage-hike impact in Q4 and not carrying into Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI-led deal ramp and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-led deals are in two categories: AI-led technology deals (legacy modernisation, AI testing, managed services) and early AI use-case deployments; margins are in line with current gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company use its growing cash?
qa_highlights.answer: M&A will focus on domain and vertical capabilities rather than digital periphery, with smaller AI investments and larger partnerships with AI players.

qa_highlights.question: What is the headcount and utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount growth is expected to be slower than revenue growth, so revenue per resource should improve; utilisation was 80% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO of 73 days sustainable, and what is the fixed-price share?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects DSO to stay in a stable range near 73 days over the long term, with short-term variation of a few days; about 40% of the business is fixed-price, and North America is above 50-55%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp-up timing for the ATLAS, FCA and Biometric deals?
qa_highlights.answer: FCA is ramping with more than 60 onsite resources and should be fully ramped by end Q1 FY27; ATLAS and Biometric are renewals with expanded scope, with ramp-up expected between Q1 and Q2 FY27.

risks_watch: Revenue conversion of the 12-month backlog ($300.4 million, +13.5% YoY in USD) depends on book-and-ship in FY27, which management is taking with caution given macro volatility and AI-led pricing pressure.
Renewal pricing: renewals are priced very competitively, earlier at 10-15% discounts and possibly much higher, which could pressure revenue and margin on existing contracts.
North America: 12-month backlog has not risen significantly despite a second quarter of positive order-book growth; revenue growth in the region is guided only as positive in FY27.
AMEA and Middle East: new decision-making has slowed due to geopolitical turbulence, and the Q4 AMEA revenue included about $0.5 million of deferred WAR revenue, a one-off.
Healthcare and Life Sciences: Q4 sequential dip from project go-live timing gaps in UK and US, with recovery dependent on new programmes starting.
Margin: management guides 16% to 16.1% EBITDA, balancing AI-led efficiency against price pressure and new AI investment; wage-hike impact is fully in Q4 and not carried into Q1 per management.
Cash deployment: M&A focus on domain and vertical assets and smaller AI investments; no specific target or deal disclosed yet. Monitor for acquisitions using the INR938 crore cash balance.
Labour Code: the INR23.7 crore Q4 true-up plus INR6.4 crore in Q3 is now classified below EBITDA; watch for any further adjustments and the restated Q3 EBITDA of 16.8%.
key_quotes: Our Q4 results has been a stable quarter.
So usually, we don't give guidance on future numbers.
The FCA deal has already started ramping up.
The renewals clearly are being extremely price competitive.
So we definitely have a stronger foundation as we enter into FY27.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book, the UK, and financial services, and on FY27 being a growth year, but cautious on quantification: it declined to give a numerical growth target, citing an unstable macro and AI-led pricing pressure. Answers on North America and AMEA were directionally optimistic, while the Middle East and renewal pricing were framed as ongoing headwinds.

growth.why: Management gives no numerical FY27 revenue guidance, only that FY27 will be better than FY26 and revenue should track the 12-month backlog, which rose 13.5% YoY in USD to $300.4M; no new capacity is being added, and utilisation is 80%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin at 16% to 16.1% (vs 16.1% in Q4 and 15.8% FY26), so only marginal expansion; wage hike fully in Q4 and not carried into Q1, but AI investment and renewal price pressure (earlier renewals at 10-15% discounts) offset gains.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches discussed; headcount rose only 54 QoQ to 4,730 and management expects headcount growth slower than revenue, so growth comes from productivity, not capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27 (H1 FY27 ramps: FCA fully ramped by end Q1 FY27; ATLAS
rows.why: 12-month backlog $300.4M, up 13.5% YoY in USD, and management says FY27 will be better than FY26 (FY26 USD growth was 3.1%), with revenue to track the backlog, though no number was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 80% (up 3.3pp QoQ) but management is redirecting cash of INR938 crore to M&A and AI partnerships rather than fixed capex; no capex plan discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give numerical guidance, citing unstable macro and AI-led pricing pressure; North America guided only to positive growth in FY27 with backlog not rising significantly.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Middle East decision-making has slowed, AMEA Q4 included a one-off ~$0.5M deferred WAR revenue, Healthcare & Life Sciences dipped on go-live gaps, and renewals are being priced at 10-15%+ discounts.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific product or brand launch discussed; AI work is described as early and small (AI share of order book about 9%, average deal about $1M) with larger partnerships instead.

rows.label: FCA deal ramp to full strength
rows.why: FCA deal has 60+ onsite resources and is due to be fully ramped by end Q1 FY27, supporting FS-led growth.

rows.label: DSO held near 73 days
rows.why: DSO fell to 73 days, lowest in 12 quarters, and management expects it to hold near that level with a swing of a few days.

rows.label: M&A and AI partnerships using INR938 crore cash
rows.why: Cash rose 51% YoY to INR938 crore and management is evaluating domain-focused M&A and larger AI partnerships, but no target or deal has been disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, UK, financial services and FY27 being a growth year, but declined to give a numerical target citing unstable macro and AI-led pricing pressure; analysts pressed on the renewal pricing, North America backlog and the margin outlook.
